Bug_Details:
Reported as "Invariant Call" by loop-hoisting.

We report this issue type when a function call is loop-invariant and hoistable, i.e.

the function has no side side effects (pure)
has invariant arguments and result (i.e. have the same value in all loop iterations)
it is guaranteed to execute, i.e. it dominates all loop sources

int foo(int x, int y) { return x + y;}void invariant_hoist(int size) {    int x = 10;    int y = 5;    for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {      foo(x, y); // hoistable    }  }
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by calling the function `foo(x, y)` inside a loop where both `x` and `y` are invariant (do not change with each iteration). The function `foo` is pure and has no side effects, making the call loop-invariant and hoistable.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggers the bug by calling the `showBug` method of the `InvariantCallExample` class. This method internally calls `invariant_hoist`, which contains the loop-invariant call to `foo(x, y)`. Since the arguments `x` and `y` do not change within the loop, the call to `foo(x, y)` is hoistable, violating the INVARIANT_CALL rule.
